title: $\alpha_f$ is an isomorphism for every $f$
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be any morphism of
schemes. Then $\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ ([def-sfb-alpha]) is
an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Let $c_f\colon f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ be the natural isomorphism of
[def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso]. By [def-sfb-alpha],
$\alpha_f=(c_f)_{\Lambda}$. Put $\beta_f=(c_f^{-1})_{\Lambda}$.
Evaluating $c_f^{-1}\circ c_f=\mathrm{id}$ and
$c_f\circ c_f^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$ at $\Lambda$ gives
$\beta_f\circ\alpha_f=\mathrm{id}_{f^*\Lambda_Y}$ and
$\alpha_f\circ\beta_f=\mathrm{id}_{\Lambda_X}$, respectively.
Thus $\beta_f$ is a two-sided inverse to $\alpha_f$.
